1x4k:
The Bachelor of Arts in Business Management and Finance provides students with a strong understanding of the crucial factors within the business sector alongside an in-depth knowledge of the key aspects of accounting and finance.

Graduates will have opportunities to work on live business projects with real-world clients, as they apply knowledge to produce creative solutions and develop confidence, business knowledge, critical thinking, and resilience to prepare them for their future career.

The University of Chichester's varied work placement opportunities help develop students' confidence, experience, and their ability to stand out from the crowd in a competitive job market. These placements will improve their employability further and act as a fantastic way to put theory into practice.
1x73:
The Bachelor of Arts in Media and Communications examines the role, influence, and evolution of the media in the University of Chichester's technologically-reliant world, as students consider the development of instant information and emerging distrust in mainstream media sources.

This industry-facing course with a mix of theory, history, and practical training opportunities allows graduates to critically analyze how the media reflects and influences people's political, personal, social, and cultural landscapes.

Graduates will develop their critical analysis and employability skills to prepare for work in media and the creative industries, graduating with highly marketable skills and a specific media knowledge. This degree focuses on developing their self-reflection and practical workplace skills, which they can put into practice on a work placement as part of the course.
1x3q:
The Bachelor of Arts in Social Work is approved by Social Work England and prepares students for a career in an exciting, challenging and fulfilling profession.

The University of Chichester welcomes a range of students with varying backgrounds, whether they are a college leaver or a mature student. They will gain a combination of effective and relevant skills alongside up-to-date knowledge of how to work effectively with children, adults and a wide range of social issues.

The course begins with a carefully structured induction program, before graduates move on to study modules designed to develop their personal and professional skills. They will be supported throughout by a structured tutorial program; linking university-based learning to practice placements.
6z4c:
Students will develop their understanding of the law and boost their employability with Master of Laws (LLM) degree. This year-long course will solidify their knowledge in criminal law and the criminal justice system, looking at contemporary issues and practice.

Graduates will hone their research, academic writing and critical thinking skills with modules including Theory of Criminal Justice, Criminal Law and Domestic and Global Terrorism. They will complete a dissertation on an area of their choice, supported by the University of Chichester expert academics.

Extra-curricular opportunities include pro bono work, mediation, work experience in a law firm or mini pupillage, in addition to mooting competitions, client-interviewing competitions and contributing to the University of Chichester Student Law Review.

This postgraduate degree will prepare students for a career within the criminal justice system or within law more widely.
1x5w:
The Master of Arts in Social Work prepares students for a wide range of experiences and learning opportunities that they will encounter in practice.

Students will gain a combination of effective and relevant skills alongside up-to-date knowledge of how to work effectively with children, adults and a wide range of social problems.

This course begins with a carefully structured induction program, before graduates move on to study modules designed to develop their personal and professional skills. They will be supported throughout by a structured tutorial program; linking university-based learning to practice placements.
1x55:
The Master of Science in International Business prepares graduates to work as a business manager in an international environment. They will explore topics including strategic management, international business, global marketing, finance and accounting, behavioral economics and research methods. If candidates are looking to brush up on their business skills or to expand their current business abroad then this course is for them.

This course develops students' managerial and general business knowledge and skills. When they graduate they will have a strong grounding in international business and be well placed to pursue an international business career in a range of organizations. Students will develop the cultural awareness they need to make an impact in an international commercial environment.
5af3:
The Master of Science in International Business and Finance degree will give students a broad practical knowledge of business administration and finance in the global business context.

Graduates will explore the essential knowledge and skills they need as an international business manager, and study strategy and research modules alongside specialist finance topics. They will complete an independent research project in their final term.

The project will develop students' research, analysis, synthesis and business writing skills. They will focus on a specific business area of their choice that related to International Business and Finance.
6z45:
The Master of Business Administration is a crucial milestone for senior managers and aspiring directors, combining essential skills, knowledge, and attributes needed to lead effectively and deliver results. This course provides students with the confidence, knowledge, and skills to begin their next step towards securing a more senior or strategic role, starting a business, or becoming a consultant.

This course asks graduates to reflect on their own knowledge and experience and use in-depth research and consultancy insights on this program to examine what is it people can do, how they can deal with obstacles, and what they can achieve.

Students will begin to see the world beyond the component parts of an organization, such as Human Resource, finance, strategy, and marketing etc, and into to the wider world and the opportunities that it presents to us. They will learn to appreciate the dynamic and holistic nature of life within the organization, across its stakeholders, suppliers, and communities.
7mts:
This Executive MBA program’s ethos encourages a holistic view of organizations, emphasizing the interconnected nature of life within and beyond the organization.

By understanding this interconnectedness, students can recognize their agency, capabilities, constraints, and responsibilities towards stakeholders, the environment, and future generations.
